MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  LA VERNE
  Monday, May 4 , 2020

1.  In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 Virus , Governor Newsom issued an Executive Order that
  temporarily suspends requ irements of the Brown Act. The Council Chambers was closed to the public, La Verne
  City Council Members attended this meeting telephonically , and meeting was live streamed on the City's website.

2.  A regular meeting of the La Verne City Council was called to order by T im Hepburn at 6 :30 pm .

8.  2020-21 Paramedic Service  City Manager Russi reported on the Paramedic Service Fee for fiscal year

9.  Mayor's Request for  Mayor Hepburn asked for consideration in establishing a La Verne Re-open
  Consideration to Establish a  Mayoral Task Force for assisting businesses in their recovery process
  Reopen La Verne Mayoral Task  after the COVID -19 crises. He stated it was important for the City to start
  Force  looking on best way to help local businesses re-open safety and follow the
  proper guidelines.

  Mayor Hepburn called for public comment on this matter and waited a few
  minutes for staff to check for public comments received via email.

  Richard Bowen and Zachary Gibson , La Verne residents submitted public
  comments .

  After Council discussion , it was the consensus of the City Council that the
  City's Economic Development Committee would look into assisting the local
  business in the recovery process.

11  Council Comments  Council Member Lau thanked everyone for their public comments. She
  reported tha t the Fourth of July parade and firework show is cancelled due to
  COVID-19, and for the safety of the community. She stated that the Fourth of
  July Committee is looking at other ways the community can celebrate the
  Fourth . She thanked the Citizen Oversight Committee applicants for their
  interest on serving on the committee.

  Mayor Pro Tern Carder stated that her husband Robert Carder applied for the
  Citizen Oversight Committee to give back to community. She stated there is no
  hidden agenda why he applied . She stated that he has pulled his application
  to be considered to serve on the Citizen Oversight Committee.

  Council Member Crosby urged residents to respond to the census and to be
  counted . He also urged residents to stay safe and follow the guidelines
  regarding COVID-19. He wished all the moms a Happy Mother's Day.

  Council Member Davis also urged residents to respond to the census and to
  be counted. He stated it was Teacher's Appreciation week and thanked all the
  La Verne teachers for all their hard work. He wished all the moms a Happy
  Mother's Day.

  Mayor Hepburn thanked City Manager Russi for his efforts on keeping the
  community safe and the COVID-19 updates on the City's website. He reported
  that Kenny Richie was selected to serve on a task force on how they will be re-
  opening schools . He spoke about the middle school and high school
  graduations. He stated it was extremely important to respond to resident's
  emails and he would appreciate if the Council Members would also respond to
  their emails. He wished all the moms a Happy Mother's Day.

12  Commun ity Development Block  City Manager Russi reported on the Community Development Block Grant
  Grant Program - Business  Program - Business Assistance Program . He went on to report on the
  Assistance Program  proposed business assistance program . He stated that the City Council
  recently approved the use of 2020-2021 Community Development Block
  Grant funds. The City Council also expressed interest for staff to explore ways
  to use CDBG funds to help businesses during the COVID-19 epidemic. Staff
  has been working closely with the Los Angeles County Development
  Authority to find a program that might work for La Verne.

  The City Council were all in favor of staff drafting program guidelines for a new
  "Business Assistance Program" that would be funded with CDBG money and
  that be brought back before Council at a later date.

Meeting Public comment

Open Letter to Councilwoman Robin Carder copied to the other Council Members, City Manager and
City Clerk--Action Required

Dear Ms. Carder,

First let me thank you for your commitment of service to the Town of LaVerne through your council position
which I know you take seriously.

However, I am extremely disappointed in seeing that your husband has applied and been included in the
selection process for the Tax Measure Citizen Oversight Committee. In a town the size of LaVerne, there
are very few opportunities for citizen involvement in the local government process, so having two from one
family takes access away from other residents. Having him apply for a position on which you have an ability to
grant participation is the highest form of nepotism. I am frankly surprised that you would even consider it as
you have, on occasion, recused yourself from a vote on something for which you could have had a vested
interest. There is no better example than this.

Many citizens were very opposed to this tax increase so the value of an Oversight Committee is very important
to a significant number of LaVerne residents. To have a spouse of a council member, his skills and potential
contribution notwithstanding, is tantamount to having the fox guard the hen house. No matter how sincere and
even handed he may think he could be, it is a visibly inappropriate choice. There should actually be guidelines
in the City Ordinances to prevent such dual participation in matters of legal and fiscal responsibility. I call for
his withdrawal from the selection process as it is the right thing to do!

Then to the remainder of the Council and city leadership,

I would apply the same ethical guidelines of non partisanship to the remainder of the selections.
These community citizens decide how to spend the dollars which represent a hardship to many constituents. For
these volunteers, a concern for the general welfare and even-handedness is required. Applicants who have
formerly been high ranking city employees (possibly with still an ax to grind) such as Ron Ingles, should not
hold this position. Also, anyone who participated in a group effort involved in unethical promotion of one
mayoral candidate at the expense of another's reputation with no regard to the facts or truth should be
eliminated. Are these the kinds of people we want "safeguarding" our fiscal responsibility? I think not.

The previous election was a mandate for higher transparency. lack of cronyism, and responsiveness to the
citizens. To go forward with some of these applicants is to send a signal back to the voters that the Council
"doesn't get it" yet, and some additional members of the Council will find their positions in jeopardy come the

  1
 next election, Use this opportunity to take the high road, select appropriately fair minded participants and
m9-ve foiward toward the best for La Verne.

Respectfully,
Kathryn Butler

Subject: Oversight committee

  April 29, 2020

  Re; Concern regarding the Citizen's Oversight Committee

  Greetings Honorable Mayor Tim Hepburn,

  My name is Patrick Valdez and I am a resident of the City of La Verne. I purchased my home
  over 30 years ago. I chose to settle in the City, because it was safe, quiet, well maintained, and
  the then City Council seemed to be in touch with the needs of their constituents.

  I have been employed for over 33 years. In my capacity, I have worked alongside
  representatives of 3 separate Contract Cities, as well as representatives of the Los Angeles
  County Board of Supervisors. My position also required that I attend weekly City Council
  meetings, in which I have attended hundreds.

  During the recent election campaign, I attend several of the "meet and greet" events you held in
  the area. During those events, you indicated that should you be elected, you would change the
  direction of the City and the "old ways" of doing business would no longer be acceptable. You
  promised to lead, and to hold others accountable. You indicated you believed in being honest,
  ethical, transparent etc., and I am therefore seeking your assistance and intervention.

  I also attended most of the City Council debates because I wanted to identify those persons who I
  felt would be the best fit to lead from the front and to make decisions for the betterment of the
  community.

  1
 Issues that are important to me personally was the building of homes on the Sierra-La Verne golf
course property, as well as the La Verne Measure M tax initiative. I can honestly say I was torn
with the bill, but ultimately voted in favor because I felt it was in the best interest of the City, it's
personnel and most importantly it's community members.

As I watched the council debates, I was satisfied to learn the candidates (with one exception) was
opposed to building homes on the golf course. This issue is important to me because my parents,
like many others, purchased their LV home due to the beautiful view of the course. We are
relying on Council to do the right thing and never change the conditional use permit for the golf
course property.

Furthermore, I was pleased to hear the candidates were in favor of forming a committee to
manage the LV tax initiative. Each candidate opined it was in the City's best interest the
committee be formed of community members and transparency was a top priority.

Earlier today, I was extremely disappointed to learn that Council member Carder's husband has
submitted an application requesting to be on the Oversight Committee. I am sure Mrs. Carder's
husband is very capable, but it certainly has the utmost appearance of cronyism. This is clearly a
conflict of interest and I am requesting that Mr. Carder withdraw his name immediately. This is
how the old regime conducted business and we saw the dissension it created amongst City Staff
and throughout the community.

Additionally, I am quite surprised the City of LV does not have a City Code preventing spouses
and/or family members of Council members from participating on any sort of committee. I can
honestly say that I have never witnessed a spouse of a council member being allowed to
participate on a committee in any of the City' s I have been affiliated.

In closing Mr. Mayor, I am asking that you closely review the list and remove any name(s) that
can potentially be detrimental or bring controversy upon the City of La Verne.

Respectfully submitted,
Patrick Valdez

Subject:  Regarding Citizen Oversight Committee - (Sales Tax Increase) PUBLIC COMMENT

Mayor Hepburn, Council and City Staff,

I am writing with concerns regarding a few of the 10 finalists for the sales tax increase citizen oversight
committee. The purpose of this group is to provide independent input and oversight in regards to the
utilization of the increased sale tax funds. To be most effective and beneficial, these residents need to be
qualified with strong financial expertise, as well as being able to provide input independent of the La Verne
city government. Two of the 10 finalists are too closely affiliated and may have biassed opinions that
would diminish the independence of their input.

Council member Carder, I am sure your husband is a fine man with relevant qualifications but I don't
believe a family member of council or city staff or current/retired employees can function independently to
represent citizens in overseeing the spending of our tax increase. Whether legally allowed or not, it does
not rise to the level of transparency or ethics suitable of an elected official, as family member can't be
completely unbiased without influencing one another in some way, nor is it proper that two members of a
single household both have a hand in making decisions regarding the city's financial expenditures when
other independent and well qualified residents are available. I'm appalled that the city manager said that
having a spouse on the committee is not a conflict of interest. It is not ethical or appropriate for the
defined purpose of oversight and, at the very least, looks bad and lends itself to further distrust of the city
governance. We need this committee to be independent and unentangled with the city government.

Also, I believe a few of the committee candidates have past municipal experience which is fine, as long as
they are not past employees of the City of La Verne, especially in positions that report to the city
manager. Former police chief Ingles would be too close to work in that committee without some kind of
bias. He has been involved in city leadership and the citizen's representatives in the oversight committee
should not be closely aligned with those they are considering for funding usage. Further, the former police
chief's involvement in funding a negative campaign PAC's attacks just a few months ago and promoting
such through personal video postings is additionally of concern. I strongly believe there need to be more
guidelines regarding this very important citizen oversight committee as to what the requirements are and
what the DIS-disqualifications are. It's too important to not ensure that citizens are looking at this both
independently and with expertise.

Relatives of city officials, both elected and/or employed, are not the best options for a transparent
oversight committee. The same is true of past employees. The committee is best suited for regular
citizens without ties that could lead to bias. I request that citizen's oversight committee be completely
above board and without city entanglements and that the two individuals I have mentioned should be
removed from the eligibility list.

Please reply to acknowledge receipt and read during Public Comment, before this item is voted on.

 Due to the worldwide pandemic of the coronavirus, the Board of Supervisors issued a strong stay-at-
home order for all of LA County that encouraged residents to stay home and work remotely, if possible .
That order has been in effect for six weeks and has been extended to May 15th . Substantial progress has
been made by our dedicated health care workers to limit the spread of the coronavirus and to treat and
assist those who have contracted the illness. As the County looks ahead and prepares to ease the stay-
at-home order and allow businesses to reopen under certain restrictions, we strongly urge you to
consider that there are many communities in Los Angeles County that have had very few reported cases
of the COVID-19 virus and that a one-size-fits-all approach to reopening is harmful to businesses and city
governments who are struggling.

There have been very limited cases reported in the eastern San Gabriel Valley. As ofTuesday, April 28 th
th ere were only 16 reported cases in the City of La Verne, which has a population of 32,206. As a
percenta ge of population, the reported infections comprise only 0.0005%. There have been only 22
reported cases in Claremont, a city with 36,478 residents (0.0006%) . In San Dimas, 27 total cases in a city
of 33,982 (0.0008%). Similar small percentages can be found in communities such as Diamond Bar,
Walnut, and La Puente. Even the City of Pomona, which has 151 confirmed cases, still has a rate of
0.0009% given their large population of 152,361.

In short, we strongly believe that a one-size-fits-all continuation of the stay-at-home order will harm
these communities which have clearly demonstrated that they have very few cases of the coronavirus
given their populations. Easing stay-at-home restrictions and allowing businesses to resume normal
operations while following strict guidelines on social distancing and the use of personal protection
equipment (PPE) is justified in these communities. This may not be the case in other cities of the county
where the stay-at-home order may need to continue until June or longer.

The longer businesses are required to remain closed or operate on a severely restricted basis, the harder
it will be for them to reopen and resume normal operations. While all of us are concerned with the
health and safety of our families and neighbors, easing these restrictions will help many struggling
businesses and their employees get back to work. We urge the Board of Supervisors to allow these
communities to be exempted from extensions of the County stay-at-home order.
